scholarships.name: Full Tuition Fee Waiver — SC/ST/PwD category
scholarships.eligibility: UG B.Tech students (excluding DASA-General, DASA-CIWG, SII, ICCR seats and the 5-year Integrated M.Sc.) and B.Sc-B.Ed students admitted under SC, ST or PwD category, regardless of family income.
scholarships.benefit: The full per-semester tuition fee is waived for the entire programme duration; hostel, mess and other charges still apply.

sources.title: Total Fee Structure for UG Programs, Academic Year 2026-2027 (Note 2)
sources.publisher: NIT Warangal — Office of the Dean (Academic)

scholarships.name: Tuition Fee Concession by Family Income — Open/EWS/OBC category
scholarships.eligibility: UG B.Tech (same exclusions as above) and B.Sc-B.Ed students of Open, EWS or OBC category whose total family income from all sources is up to Rs 5 lakh a year.
scholarships.benefit: Full tuition fee waiver when annual family income is below Rs 1 lakh; two-thirds of the tuition fee waived when income is between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 5 lakh a year.

scholarships.name: NSP Top Class Education Scholarship for SC Students
scholarships.eligibility: First-year SC B.Tech students admitted on institute CRL rank with family income up to Rs 8 lakh a year; NIT Warangal gets a fixed yearly quota of fresh slots (16 in 2023-24), 30% reserved for girls by merit; renewal is subject to satisfactory academic progress.
scholarships.benefit: Full tuition-fee waiver, plus (fresh year only) a one-time other-fee reimbursement and laptop allowance, and an annual living-expense plus books/stationery allowance every year. In 2023-24 this totalled about Rs 86,000 (fresh) or Rs 41,000/year (renewal).

sources.title: Scheme-wise Guidelines for National Scholarship Portal (NSP) 2023-24 — Top Class Scholarship for SC Students (p. 3), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

scholarships.name: Institute Merit-cum-Means (MCM) Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: UG 1st, 2nd and 3rd year B.Tech students who are provisionally shortlisted by the Academic Section each year on a combined merit-and-means basis; awardees submit an acquittance roll confirming they hold no other scholarship or full tuition-fee waiver for the same year.
